A: side vectors (4,4), (-4,4), (-4,-4), (4,-4); every side has length sqrt(32); (4,4).(-4,4) = 0, so A has right angles.

D: side vectors (2,1) and (-2,4); (2,1).(-2,4) = 0; lengths sqrt(5) and 2*sqrt(5), so D is a rectangle with a long side twice the short side.

diagram.manim_description: On a plain BG 16:9 canvas draw two panels stacked top to bottom, both centred on the same vertical axis, fitted uniformly to the canvas with a 4% margin, using cm with x to the right and y upward. Top panel: a rectangle in INK, stroke width 3 px, with corners (0,10), (9,10), (9,13), (0,13), divided by two vertical INK lines at x = 3 and x = 6 running from y = 10 to y = 13, so it holds three squares of side 3 cm; draw no vertex letters. Write 9 cm in INK centred at (4.5, 14.3) above a double-headed INK arrow at y = 13.7 running from x = 0 to x = 9. Write 3 cm in INK centred at (1.5, 9.4), at (4.5, 9.4) and at (7.5, 9.4), below the three squares. Write 3 cm in INK centred at (-1.3, 11.5), left of a double-headed INK arrow at x = -0.6 running from y = 10 to y = 13. Bottom panel: a rectangle ACDF in INK, stroke width 3 px, with corners F (0.5,2) bottom-left, D (8.5,2) bottom-right, C (8.5,6) top-right, A (0.5,6) top-left, divided by a vertical INK line from B (4.5,6) to E (4.5,2). Write the letters A above-left of A, B above B, C above-right of C, F below-left of F, E below E and D below-right of D in INK. Draw one short tick of length 0.3 cm in ANSWER, perpendicular to the segment, at the midpoint of each of the seven segments AB, BC, FE, ED, AF, BE and CD. Write 8 cm in INK centred at (4.5, 7.9) above a double-headed INK arrow at y = 7.3 running from x = 0.5 to x = 8.5. Write 4 cm in INK centred at (-0.9, 4), left of a double-headed INK arrow at x = -0.1 running from y = 2 to y = 6. Draw nothing else: no compass, no arcs, no ruler.
must_not_show: headings, Q-numbers, figure letters like a. or b.
compass, arcs, ruler or construction steps
vertex letters on the top panel
accuracy_checks: Top panel: three squares of side 3 cm, 3 + 3 + 3 = 9 cm total length, height 3 cm, so length = 3 x breadth.
Bottom panel: AF = 4 cm (A (0.5,6), F (0.5,2)); AB = BC = 4 cm, so AC = 4 + 4 = 8 cm and the rectangle is 8 cm by 4 cm.
ABEF and BCDE are squares of side 4 cm: AF = AB = BE = FE = BC = CD = ED = 4 cm, one tick on each of these seven segments.
Both panels are drawn at the same scale (1 cm is the same length in both).
diagram.alt_text: Two drawings: a 9 cm by 3 cm rectangle split into three squares of side 3 cm, and an 8 cm by 4 cm rectangle ACDF split into two squares ABEF and BCDE with equal-side ticks.
diagram.render_note: One diagram for the two blocks that share this card (the pair gets one solution diagram). The first block's printed answer is only a hint ('take the length three times the breadth'); the LP answer gives the example 9 cm by 3 cm. The second panel is the book's rough diagram (page 14: 7 ticks on AB, BC, FE, ED, AF, BE, CD) with the 4 cm and 8 cm values of the LP answer. The first panel carries no vertex letters because the LP steps letter only the first square (AB, AD, BC).

diagram.manim_description: On a plain BG 16:9 canvas draw a rectangle 8 cm wide and 4 cm tall in INK, stroke width 3 px, to scale, placed with its lower-left corner at 30.4% of the canvas width from the left and 75.7% of the canvas height from the top, with 1 cm equal to 12.25% of the canvas height; use cm with that corner at the origin, x to the right and y upward, so the corners are (0,0), (8,0), (8,4), (0,4). Draw two vertical INK lines inside it, one at x = 2 and one at x = 6, each running from y = 0 to y = 4, so the rectangle shows a left strip 2 cm wide, a square 4 cm by 4 cm in the middle and a right strip 2 cm wide. Draw a double-headed INK arrow at y = 4.8 from x = 0 to x = 8 and write 8 cm in INK centred at (4, 5.4). Draw a double-headed INK arrow at x = -0.8 from y = 0 to y = 4 and write 4 cm in INK centred at (-1.7, 2). Leave the inner lines unlabelled. Draw nothing else: no letters, no shading, no gap measures.
must_not_show: headings, Q-numbers, figure letters like a. or b.
the 2 cm gaps or the 4 cm side of the inner square
the centre of the rectangle or any construction mark
accuracy_checks: Inner lines at x = 2 and x = 6: the middle part is 6 - 2 = 4 cm wide and 4 cm tall, so it is a square that touches the top and the bottom.
Left strip 2 cm and right strip 2 cm: equal, so the centre of the square (4,2) is the centre of the rectangle (4,2).
Rectangle drawn 2 : 1 (8 cm by 4 cm); the book's own picture is slightly off scale (about 2.2 : 1).
